claims: C1 whether an item of information counts as private or sensitive is not settled by the information alone; it depends on the context the information arises in
C2 the dependence is partial: context is one of the things that settle the question and not the whole of it, so context alone does not settle it either

concepts.name: privacy_context_dependence
concepts.gloss: whether the item of information in the first argument counts as private or sensitive is settled only partly by the second argument, the context it arises in - the information on its own does not settle the question, and neither does the context on its own

concepts.name: occurs_in_context
concepts.gloss: the first argument is an item of information at issue in the situation being judged and the second is the surrounding setting it is asked for or disclosed in - who is asking, in what setting, and what has already been said
concepts.inference: for information to depend on context, each item of information at issue must stand in some relation to a context; the span presupposes that relation without naming it

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule belonging to the protect-privacy section of the document, and the authority level it carries is the root level rather than one of the lower levels other material is held at
concepts.inference: this is a borrowed name another node establishes; the meaning recorded here is the one the node contract hands over, and the narrowed span itself says nothing about sections or authority levels
